conventions.convention: The classical register uses reduced separated finite-type spaces over an algebraically closed field, allowing reducible and empty varieties; irreducible varieties are nonempty.
A normal point has an integrally closed domain as its germ ring. Normality allows reducible varieties, but distinct components cannot meet at a normal point.
Finiteness requires affine inverse images with module-finite coordinate algebras, is affine-local on the target, and allows empty inverse images with zero coordinate ring.

Codimension-one regularity and pole tests use height-one prime localizations on affine charts, not only classical closed-point germ rings. Empty intersections in dimension zero mean the common function field.
Normal and regular integral curves agree without perfectness; equivalence with smoothness requires a perfect ground field.
Elementary étale changes use square standard-smooth presentations and selected classical points with residue field k. Tensor-product base changes retain nilpotents.
Multiplicative type and tori are defined by fpqc-local splitting, without assuming affineness or separable splitting. Finite-type nonsmooth groups are allowed, and rank-zero tori are included.
Character modules are finitely generated discrete abelian groups with continuous Galois action. Transport acts by σ(c e_m)=σ(c)e_{σm}, and group morphisms reverse character-module morphisms.

Intersection multiplicity is ambient-local-ring length. Its curve argument is integral of dimension one, and its generic point must avoid the second subscheme. The blowup-drop lemma additionally requires regularity of that curve at the center.

A regular surface has pure dimension two and regular local rings; smoothness over a field is not required. A closed center of local dimension one has identity blowup and point exceptional subscheme; a dimension-two center has exceptional P¹ over its residue field.
Finite normalization is an explicit hypothesis for arbitrary integral Noetherian curves. Regularization permits the empty sequence and otherwise chooses nonregular closed centers.

SNC means reduced support with regular irreducible components, at most two through a point, and intersection length one when two meet. The total transform may have multiplicities, and crossing support need not itself be regular.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC and k algebraically closed. For a separated finite-type morphism with finite fibres between classical varieties, allowing reduced reducible or empty varieties, the affine relative integral closures glue to a finite classical morphism ν:N→Y, and evaluation glues to an open immersion j:X→N with f=ν∘j.

Assume AC. For an integral Noetherian scheme Y of dimension one and a closed point p, Bl_p(Y)→Y is finite, is an isomorphism off p, and is an isomorphism if and only if O_{Y,p} is regular, equivalently its maximal ideal is invertible.

Assume AC. Let X be locally Noetherian, Y,Z closed, and p∈Y∩Z closed, with Y integral of dimension one, η_Y∉Z, and O_{Y,p} regular. After blowing up p, Y′→Y is an isomorphism, Y′ meets the exceptional subscheme in one point q with intersection multiplicity one, and if q∈Z′ then m_q(Y′∩Z′)<m_p(Y∩Z). Multiplicity one therefore gives disjoint strict transforms over p.

Assume AC. An irreducible classical variety over an algebraically closed field has a finite surjective birational normalization from a normal variety, obtained by gluing affine integral closures inside the common function field and independent of the affine cover. Reduced reducible varieties are normalized componentwise by disjoint union.

Assume AC. Over an arbitrary field k, G↦X*(G) is a contravariant equivalence between finite-type multiplicative-type group schemes and finitely generated abelian groups with continuous Γ_k-action; its inverse has coordinate algebra (k_s[M])^{Γ_k}, with σ(c e_m)=σ(c)e_{σm}. No smoothness, connectedness, perfection, or characteristic-zero hypothesis is required.
Assume AC. Let k_s be a separable closure of an arbitrary field k. Every finite-type multiplicative-type group over k is diagonalizable over k_s and over a finite Galois subextension L/k of k_s/k.

For finite Galois L/k with group Γ, a commutative Hopf L-algebra B with semilinear Γ-action preserving its Hopf maps descends to A=B^Γ, with L⊗_k A≅B. Finite generation and equivariant Hopf maps descend; canonical scalar extensions recover their original fixed algebra.

Assume AC. For an integral Noetherian one-dimensional Y with finite normalization ν:Y^ν→Y and closed p, ν factors uniquely through the finite blowup β:Bl_p(Y)→Y. Y^ν remains its normalization, and β_*O embeds as a coherent O_Y-subalgebra of ν_*O_{Y^ν}.

Assume AC. Blowing up a nonregular closed point of an integral Noetherian one-dimensional scheme with finite normalization strictly increases its pushed-forward structure subalgebra inside the fixed normalization. The first-step quotient is nonzero coherent of finite length supported exactly at the center; composite pushforwards strictly increase at every subsequent nonregular-center step.
On a Noetherian scheme X, an increasing sequence F₁⊆F₂⊆⋯ of coherent submodules of a coherent O_X-module F stabilizes. The proof inherits AC through the affine quasi-coherent interface.

Assume AC. An integral Noetherian one-dimensional scheme with finite normalization admits a finite sequence of closed-point blowups ending in a regular curve. Centers may all be nonregular, giving strict increases of coherent subalgebras inside the fixed finite normalization; an already regular curve permits the empty sequence.

Assume AC. Blowing up a closed point of a locally Noetherian regular surface of pure dimension two preserves regularity and pure dimension two. The exceptional subscheme is effective Cartier: P¹_{κ(p)} when dim O_{S,p}=2, and the reduced point with identity blowup when dim O_{S,p}=1. The blowup is an isomorphism off the center.

Assume AC and k algebraically closed. For separated finite-type finite-fibre classical f:X→Y, C_U=Int_{k[U]}Γ(f^{-1}U,O_X) is finite reduced and commutes with principal localization. These algebras glue to finite N→Y and evaluation gives X→N. Sections commute with flat finite-type affine base change, retaining nilpotents.

Assume AC. For reduced finite-type A over algebraically closed k, any A-algebra B, C=Int_A(B), and an elementary étale change A→E, E⊗_A C injects into E⊗_A B and equals Int_E(E⊗_A B). B need not be finite type, reduced, or a domain.

Assume AC. A finite morphism f:X→Y of finite-type schemes over any field, with Y projective, admits a closed immersion into P^N_Y and has projective source over the field. Finite morphisms are separated, finite type, and universally closed; no local freeness of f_*O_X is assumed.

Assume AC. On an irreducible normal classical variety over an algebraically closed field, a rational function is globally regular exactly when it belongs to every height-one prime localization on every affine chart. The intersections are inside k(X), with empty dimension-zero intersection interpreted as k(X).

concerns.concern: Scope wording needs clarification. The Statement says 'Affine k-group schemes are contravariantly equivalent to commutative Hopf k-algebras' without a finite-generation restriction. Its preceding owned definition says group schemes follow def-group-scheme-over-a-field, which defines only 'a group scheme of finite type over k'. Arbitrary Hopf algebras and D_k(M) for arbitrary abelian M require the unrestricted affine group-scheme category. The proof establishes that unrestricted dictionary; explicitly distinguish it from the finite-type convention, or state the corresponding finite-generation restriction.

seams_checked.note: Opened the supplier page and def-group-scheme-over-a-field. The finite-type multiplicative-type objects retain the group-object scheme structure and allow nilpotents without reducedness or smoothness. The unrestricted auxiliary Hopf-category wording is separately recorded as an owned presentation concern.

Opened the supplier page and cited item statements, plus the normalization and Euler-drop proofs. Consumers preserve finite-type center ideals, localized Rees charts, saturated strict transforms, flat base change, intrinsic curve blowups, and universal-property Cartier hypotheses. Field normalization is invoked only in finite-type field examples; arbitrary Noetherian curves separately assume finite normalization. The cusp Euler formula retains properness, ampleness, residue degree, multiplicity, and its decreasing-defect sign.

Opened the supplier page, thm-nonaffine-regular-local-ring-is-ufd, and its principal-localization Picard supplier. The consumed proposition is exactly that every regular local ring is a UFD under AC. Consumers apply it to regular local rings without imposing a ground field or confusing regularity with smoothness.
